dialogue.content: I spent the first hour tidying the argument outline and closing stale entries.
Anything still open?
Two items, both with owners.
The court calendar review wrapped early today.
Any surprises in it?
None worth recording.
I can answer a judge's procedural question in a brief hearing.
That is not a full mock argument.
No, it does not require sustained projection or repetition.
Someone new shadowed me in the advocacy room this morning.
Did that slow you down?
A little, but the questions were good ones.
I batched my replies about the trial-prep weeks into one message before lunch.
Cleaner than drip-feeding answers.
Much cleaner.
I did a standard pass over the court calendar records this morning.
Any exceptions in there?
None worth a note.
I prepare trainees with a written objection map and recorded examples.
Can they use those before a live practice?
Yes, live time can focus on the few contested exchanges.
I archived last cycle's notes on the court calendar and set up the new folder.
A fresh start?
As fresh as these things get.
I confirmed next week's court calendar slots with the team.
Any conflicts?
None that survived five minutes.
A vendor call about the argument outline ran long but ended well.
Worth the time?
This one, yes.
I walked through the advocacy room checklist with the new starter.
How did they do?
Careful and quick, a good sign.
Quiet afternoon; I cleared the backlog around the trial-prep weeks.
A rare day.
I did not waste it.
I flagged a small inconsistency in the court calendar records and fixed it at the source.
Root cause or symptom?
Root cause, for once.
I closed a routine trial-prep weeks cycle without surprises.
Follow-up needed?
A note for the next cycle, nothing more.
I sketched next week's plan for the trial-prep weeks before leaving.
Ahead of schedule?
Ahead enough to sleep well.
Lunch walk, then a clean pass through the argument outline updates.
Does the walk help?
It resets the afternoon.
I moved my reminders so the argument outline review lands before the weekly sync.
Small automation helps.
It adds up over a quarter.
I compared two options for the court calendar tooling and noted a mild preference.
Decision made?
Deferred until the trial ends.
I closed the week by updating the advocacy room handover notes.
Anything unusual to hand over?
Blessedly little.
For Thursday, should I rank two full mock arguments above a single targeted practice before Friday's 09:00 evidentiary hearing?
